[MUQATIL:26:160-173/r10] MUQATIL, d. 150 · قوم لوط | reports | Lot’s people threaten to expel him from the town unless he stops speaking against them.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابms925ماتقلبفيهالسينصادافيبعضاللغات)#811/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | When qāf follows sīn in the same word, some speakers replace sīn with ṣād, as in صقت and صبقت, because qāf's retracted articulation pulls it upward.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابms925ماتقلبفيهالسينصادافيبعضاللغات)#811/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Ṣād is chosen because it is the closest match to qāf's upward articulation; this resembles ط in مصطبر and د in مزدجر, despite intervening sounds.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابms925ماتقلبفيهالسينصادافيبعضاللغات)#811/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The intervening sounds do not block the shift; Sībawayh compares it with imāla of alif in forms such as صار, طار, and غزا.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابms925ماتقلبفيهالسينصادافيبعضاللغات)#811/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Ḫāʾ and ġayn act like qāf in this process, as in صالغ for سالغ and صلخ for سلخ.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابms925ماتقلبفيهالسينصادافيبعضاللغات)#811/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | No parallel shift occurs with zāy before qāf: zāy is voiced and does not rise like voiceless ṣād.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابms925ماتقلبفيهالسينصادافيبعضاللغات)#811/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · بنو العنبر | reports | Banu al-Anbar say صاطع, with ṣād before ṭāʾ, since ṭāʾ shares the upward articulation and is closer.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابms925ماتقلبفيهالسينصادافيبعضاللغات)#811/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Sīn and ṣād match in voicelessness, whistling, and frication; the sound changes to a counterpart matching in all features except emphatic articulation.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابms925ماتقلبفيهالسينصادافيبعضاللغات)#811/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The proposed ذ-to-ظ shift is rejected: ذ is less close to qāf, and the sīn shift is already exceptional; tāʾ and thāʾ likewise lack the same conditions before dāl.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p520/r2] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · author | holds | They threaten to expel Lot from their town, meaning they will kill him and carry him out dead.
[THALABI:v7p177/r1] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | Lot's people are transgressors because they go beyond what is lawful to what is forbidden.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p112/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | Here it means if Lot does not stop speaking.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p112/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | They threaten to expel Lot from their town and village.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p112/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | The threat parallels what the people told Shuʿayb in 7:88. | mentions 7:88
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:165-168/r4] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | They threaten to drive Lot out of their town if he does not stop.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p126/r7] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | Lot's people threaten to expel him from their town.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p240#3/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | They threaten to expel Lūṭ from his land and home; he answers simply that he detests their deed.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p140#4/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | They threaten Lot that if he does not stop reproaching them, they will expel him from their town.
[RAZI-FULL:v24p138#2/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The threat means that Lot would be among those expelled from their town; they may have driven people out in the worst possible conditions.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:26:167-171/r1] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | They threaten Lot to stop either what he claims or their condemnation and prohibition of their conduct.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:26:167-171/r2] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | They threaten to expel Lot from their midst, likely by driving him out violently and humiliatingly.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p195#10/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | They tell Lot to stop condemning and reproaching their conduct.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p195#10/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | They threaten to expel him from among them and drive him from their town, perhaps in the harshest manner.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p183/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | The threat means they will expel Lot as they expelled earlier people who forbade the act, or any dissenter whatever the issue.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | When Lūṭ forbade their lewd approach to males and directed them to their wives, they threatened expulsion unless he stopped preaching.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | The threat meant that they would drive Lūṭ out from among them.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Their threat echoes the people's response in 7:82: to expel Lūṭ and his followers because they claimed to be pure. | mentions 7:82
[NASHR:v1p222/r1] NASHR, d. 833 · author | holds | Mīm is nasal; avoid emphatic coloring when it is vocalized, especially before emphatic letters or alif. Its ghunna comes from the nose when it is assimilated or sākin.
[NASHR:v1p222/r2] NASHR, d. 833 · author | holds | A sākin mīm is assimilated with ghunna before another mīm, as in doubled mīm forms.
[NASHR:v1p222/r3] NASHR, d. 833 · author | prefers | Before bāʾ, al-Dani, Ibn Mujahid, and western performance traditions prefer hiding the sākin mīm with ghunna; others, including Makki, and eastern traditions choose full izhar. The author accepts both but prefers ikhfāʾ; Ahmad ibn Yaqub reports consensus for izhar.
[NASHR:v1p222/r4] NASHR, d. 833 · author | holds | A sākin mīm is pronounced clearly before all remaining letters; take particular care before fāʾ or wāw, keeping it still rather than letting the tongue hide or vocalize it.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p383/r11] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | They swear that if Lot does not stop his protest, they will expel him in a degrading public fashion.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p383/r12] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Addressing him by name instead of an honorific is deliberately harsh and coarse.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p383/r13] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | They want personally to expel this outsider to humiliate him and be rid of objections, following their custom of exiling critics; God instead brings him out honorably through angels.
[BURSEVI:v6p219#2/r1] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Lot’s people threaten him to stop condemning and denouncing their conduct.
[BURSEVI:v6p219#2/r2] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | They threaten to expel him from the town violently and disgracefully, as one marked for exile.
[ALUSI-FULL:v19p116/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | They threaten Lot to stop rebuking and condemning them, or to stop claiming prophethood, calling them to faith, and objecting to their conduct.
[ALUSI-FULL:v19p116/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The threat means Lot will be among those expelled from their familiar town; they apparently expelled people who angered them for various reasons.
[ALUSI-FULL:v19p116/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | Another account says they expelled people who condemned their sexual obscenity harshly, explaining why they threatened Lot this way.
[ALUSI-FULL:v19p116/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The longer formulation 'you will be among the expelled' is more emphatic than the shorter 'we will expel you.'
[ELMALILI:26:160-175/r5] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | They threaten to expel Lūṭ if he does not stop.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p180/r1] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Like Noah’s people, Lot’s opponents threaten him, but they threaten expulsion because he was an immigrant from outside the town who had married into the community.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p180/r2] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The construction من المخرجين is more emphatic than saying لنخرجنك, as with من المرجومين in Noah’s story. | mentions 26:116
[TABATABAI:26:167-175/r2] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | They threaten to expel Lot from their town, as their other statement makes explicit: drive Lot's family out of the town. | mentions 27:56
[TABATABAI:26:167-175/r4] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Lot answers their threat without addressing it, signaling that he does not fear exile; he despises their deed and wants to escape its inevitable punishment.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p441/r6] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | Their wording makes the threat a decisive warning, not an empty threat; although they had threatened earlier, this time they meant to carry it out.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:167/r1] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | The people threaten Lot that if he does not stop, he too will be expelled.
[QIRAAT-ER:26:167:11#1/r1] QIRAAT-ER · Ḥafṣ | reports | The standard Ḥafṣ form is a passive participle from Form IV kh-r-j, and the source says it is universal across major transmissions.
[STUDYQURAN:26:167/r1] STUDYQURAN · author | holds | The threat to expel Lot is cross-referenced with the parallel account at 7:82. | mentions 7:82
